mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last four weeks (-9.7 to -3.3), reflecting a self-reinforcing recovery in discretionary outings. This momentum should continue without new shocks, pushing the next-28-day mean above the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:monotonic weekly increase from -9.7 to -3.3 over last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean falls below its last-28-day mean despite the four-week monotonic uptrend persisting through the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT mobility crosses above -35 (percent change from baseline), commuter and errand-linked trips reach a density that mechanically spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -35 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -44.1 to -37.7 over four weeks, approaching -35 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the two weeks following a TRANSIT crossing above -35, or rises at a rate unrelated to the crossing event.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES (less negative) and decline in RESIDENTIAL (less positive) jointly indicate reduced at-home anchoring; their combined effect amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series predicts alone, because freed daytime hours convert into discretionary shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved -16.3 to -11.4 while RESIDENTIAL fell 6.3 to 4.0 over same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than the growth predicted from WORKPLACES or RESIDENTIAL alone, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows large week-to-week swings (-20.9, -25.1, -12.6, -7.3) consistent with a seasonal transition into warmer weather; this seasonal lift in outdoor activity co-occurs with and precedes increased retail and recreation visits as people combine outdoor trips with shopping errands.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded sharply from -25.1 to -7.3 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even as PARKS continues its upward trajectory, indicating no seasonal transmission to retail.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM (7.3 to 10.4) alongside improving WORKPLACES suggests a policy environment of loosening restrictions on essential and non-essential activity alike; this broader permissive regime extends to retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +8 for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES improves
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose monotonically from 7.3 to 10.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines over the next four weeks even though GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both continue improving, indicating the policy-linkage mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below +4.5 (percent change from baseline), it indicates a behavioral tipping point where households spend materially less time at home, directly converting into higher next-week RETAIL_REC as pent-up errands and leisure trips are executed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +4.5 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 4.0 in the most recent week, just below the 4.5 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a RESIDENTIAL reading below +4.5.

mechanism_narrative: If the week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT decelerates to less than 1 point of percent-change recovery, it signals that the commuting and transit-based recovery is stalling, which caps further gains in trip-linked retail visits and causes RETAIL_REC growth to flatten or reverse within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week improvement falls below 1 percentage point
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly gains have been decelerating (1.5, 3.5, 2.7, 2.2 points) toward the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week following a TRANSIT deceleration below 1 point, showing no link between transit stall and retail slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: Joint sustained recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over four weeks indicates a full-cycle return-to-routine (commute plus work), and their combined improvement compounds to drive a larger four-week increase in RETAIL_REC than either series individually would predict, as daily routines re-anchor around workplaces and transit hubs adjacent to retail corridors.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES (-16.3 to -11.4) and TRANSIT (-44.1 to -37.7) improved monotonically over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's four-week forward increase is no larger than the sum of increases attributable to WORKPLACES and TRANSIT individually, indicating no compounding interaction effect.
